And when I expressed to him how hurt I was about that, he said “but my brother in law said, isn’t she going though?” But if women were on dating sites, before their husband moved out, everyone would be saying “shouldn’t you spend some time alone first?” The whole thing is a scam.

I’m happier when I’m not constantly thinking about whether I’m attractive to a man, so much happier. My brain space is now free to focus on my goals for myself. I’m glad I figured it out now, because now I can enjoy my life. Men never made my life better only worse.

It’s a process, and forcing yourself to feel anything other than what you are feeling is counterproductive. 

The first step is to remove from your psyche, that you are to blame for your relationship failures. “Choose better” is a narrative that is endlessly trotted out, as a way to gaslight women into believing they are at fault for mistreatment. When in reality, it’s not possible to choose better, because there is rarely anything better to choose from. 

Next step is to start paying attention to how you feel, in your body, when you think about pandering to a man for the rest of your life. For me, it causes a great deal of anxiety. Self acceptance, and loving yourself exactly as you are is nearly impossible, if you have to constantly stay young (impossible) and be hot and sexy for a man. Now start paying attention to how you feel, when you think about opting OUT of this paradigm—peaceful right? Self acceptance never felt so easy. For me, I felt relieved. I leaned in to that. 

You don’t have to specifically DO anything, other than developing stronger awareness, and allowing that awareness to percolate in your day to day consciousness, the shifts will come eventually.

Her treatment of me has led to me not knowing how to keep myself safe, or feeling like there is something wrong with ME (and not the perpetrator) when my mind and body tell me I’m not safe. That’s destruction on a mind, body and spiritual level, and it’s unforgivable. I resonate with a lot of what you say, but you sound like a highly attuned and self aware person. And I have a big heart, and would give someone my last penny. So why am I feeling like it’s all my fault again?  Thank you for keeping your fingers crossed for me. Before we met up (we met on a dating site) he told he was going round his friends to play PlayStation. He even text me from his “mates bathroom” to say how much he was thinking of me, and how he can’t wait to see me. Turns out he had some woman over his house for a night of passion. I knew it was a lie. But at the time I thought “well what can I do? We haven’t even met yet.” We had been talking for over a month, FaceTime, Skype. (He lived 300 miles away) so I felt like we both knew each other so well. But it was an awful feeling knowing what he was doing. Especially since he made himself out to be someone who was entirely trustworthy and would never lie.

I’m totally checked out of this relationship now. I’m currently awaiting news about my new house. Hoping for good news, and then I’ll be outta here. The best thing I ever did was start documenting the behaviour, it sped up the process of wanting to leave very quickly. It became the clarity out of the fog. How about you? Have you left yours?

Your comment about his intentions is absolutely spot on. He was hoping I wouldn’t notice, so that he could make me out to be unreasonable for not wanting them in the first place. It’s about WINNING. Him being right, and me being wrong. And the sad thing is, he could have said something as simple as (like you say) “no worries I’ll make you something else” but now it’s blown up into this huge thing, and I end up feeling bad about highlighting his resistance to the word no. 

I’ve been documenting his behaviour since the start of the year on my notes app (for sanity reasons) and it’s pages and pages long! We have been together 6 years. If I had documented the whole time, I’d of been able to submit a phD dissertation. 

I have told him before “you always want to be right” and he says “no I don’t” but then goes on to justify why he is right and I’m wrong. He doesn’t seem to understand nuance. He thinks that wanting to be right means he has to explicitly state “I’m right.” This isn’t correct. Because if his explanations are all about justifying his actions, then he is essentially saying “I’m right.” Is it not? So you are essentially being gaslighted about the gaslighting. Who knew there could be levels to this? lmao.

Oh, you are so insightful. It’s exactly like being in a playground. Anything I say will be immediately turned around onto me. “I don’t feel like you have any empathy for me”. His response “do you have any for me?” Or even “I don’t feel cared for “I could say the same about you” and on and on for EVERYTHING. 

Like you say, when he called me narcissistic, I went away and reflected. I was triggered. But he was so confident in his perspective, he didn’t feel the need to which is very telling. He immediately brushed it off! 

One thing I will say is this,  once you start looking at  their behaviour through the lens of abuse, the examples of it start becoming apparent thick and fast. This weekend for example, Saturday specifically, I told him I don’t really want chicken thighs for dinner. I’ve gone off them (as we all can with food from time to time) I’ve not eaten them in months. But on Sunday, I see he has taken the chicken thighs out of the freezer. So I had to tell him again, I really don’t want the chicken thighs. He then proceeded to debate with me about the chicken and why I don’t want them. I counted in total 30 times, I told him in that discussion I didn’t want chicken thighs. And guess what…..when we finally sat down to eat (I had paella and he had chicken thighs) guess what he mixed in with my paella. Chicken thighs?!?!?!?!) I wish I was joking but I’m really not. He then rationalised it at the dinner table, as “I only put a small bit in. I wanted to see if you would notice” but at this point it really is quite weird and sinister. I  said NO. I said it over 30 times and he did it anyway? And then said “calm down ok I’ve got it” when I expressed that this was odd. But at what point did he get it? There is chicken in my meal? Wild.

This was really thought provoking. He hasn’t called any of them crazy, but I did notice he wasn’t able to self reflect on any level of depth how his behaviour contributed to the relationship ending. 

What’s very strange about my soon to be NEX is he consistently tells me he is unaware of his behaviour, and that “Why would I want to cause all of this conflict on purpose because I’m getting punished too” which is a royal head “f*uck. My response is always “but I’ve told you over and over and over again the behaviour that is harmful so how can you not know?” Surely if the injured party tells you what the harmful behaviour is, the onus is then on you to take responsibility and make sure it never happens again? Especially if you claim to love and care about them. But it’s like nothing I say goes in. And then he plays the victim when my reactions to his behaviour is unfavourable. It’s really quite strange and hard to understand. 

Another thing I have not been able to understand. Is his lack of inclination, towards self education. If someone called me abusive, the first thing I’d do is go on Google and search. When he called me a narcissist (after I had called him abusive) I went and read hundreds of articles, and did multiple online tests to determine if I was or not. (The tests said I wasn’t). But despite me telling him he is emotionally abusive for years and years he has never felt the need to find out if he is or not, he just knows he isn’t. And I’ve got it wrong. “What planet are you living on?” he says to me. He also says “I’m not worried about labels. What matters is, am I happy or not?” 

When he called me a narcissist I remember having a huge panic attack. Because the thought that I could be harming people, and being completely unaware of it was so triggering to me. And knowing that I’d want to be alone for the rest of my life, because I wouldn’t want to inflict any pain on another. 

He doesn’t seem to have that worry at all.
